title: Traffic Surge Stabilizer for Hosted API: automated slow-rolls, surge dampening, and emergency fallback
creator: Carlos Rivera
description: Background: Recent staged rollouts exposed two classes of runtime regression during regional migrations: 1) short-lived traffic spikes that cause transient KV cache thrashing and 2) oscillatory redistributions when routing weights are stepped too aggressively. This ticket designs and implements an automated 'surge stabilizer' layer in the Hosted API pipeline to dampen traffic oscillation, perform controlled slow-rolls across regions, and provide deterministic emergency fallback to the last LTS model/route.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New stabilizer component applied during rollout prevents >25% increase in p99 latency under synthetic 30% spike tests compared to baseline.
2) Weighted traffic changes are smoothed such that no more than 10% absolute weight move occurs in any 60s window unless manually overridden.
3) Automated gating will abort or pause a rollout and shift a failing region to LTS within 90s of SLO breach detection.
4) Runbook steps for manual override and rollback are documented and verified in a tabletop exercise.
5) End-to-end e2e test in staging (multi-region) exercises surge scenarios and produces green CI with metrics assertions.
tasks: Design traffic smoothing algorithm (exponential moving average with adaptive window based on request variance).
Implement stabilizer service as a control-plane microservice with idempotent APIs for set_weight/adjust_weight/drain.
Hook stabilizer into rollout controller: pre-step validation, per-step smoothing policy enforcement, emergency-fallback trigger.
Add CLI flags to rollout tool: --surge-dampen, --smoothing-window, --emergency-fallback=true.
Instrument metrics and alerts: per-region p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, token-throughput, cache-miss-rate, and stabilization-action events.
Add automated tests: unit tests for smoothing math, integration tests for staged weight transitions, chaos tests (SLO breach simulation).
Update Console UI docs and add a compact toggle for surge stabilization during rollouts.
Author and rehearse incident runbook for emergency fallback to LTS route.
test_plan: Unit: verify smoothing math preserves total weight and converges within expected time constants.
Integration: staging rollout across three simulated regions with injected latency spikes; assert metrics do not exceed thresholds in acceptance criteria.
Chaos: simulate KV cache cold-start wave combined with 2x traffic burst; ensure stabilizer drains safely and LTS fallback activates when SLOs breach.
Manual tabletop: SRE + Eng-run through runbook for fail-open and fail-safe scenarios.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Deploy stabilizer binary to control plane in staging + enable feature flag.
Phase 1: Canary run using internal tenants in one region with smoothing-window=30s and surge-dampen=0.5 for 24h.
Phase 2: Gradual regional rollouts with adaptive windows: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 4h per step, enforced by stabilizer.
Phase 3: Post-rollout verification: 24h observation with elevated metric capture; automatic rollback if any region breaches error-budget thresholds defined in SLO policy.
monitoring_checks: SLO watchers: error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 2m triggers pause-and-evaluate.
Latency cliffs: p99 increase > 20% over baseline within a 5m window triggers emergency-fallback candidate.
Cache miss spike: KV cache miss-rate > 1.5x baseline for 3m pauses weight change for region.
Stabilizer health: controller heartbeats staleness > 30s triggers circuit-breaker to stop automated moves and alert on-call.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive smoothing can stall rollouts for benign regressions. Mitigation: expose manual override and conservative default smoothing parameters.

Risk: New control-plane service becomes single point of failure. Mitigation: deploy as redundant replicas, ensure read-only local fallback in agent, and fail-open to previous stable route when control-plane unreachable.

Risk: False-positive SLO triggers during transient cloud flakiness. Mitigation: combine SLO breach detection with cluster-level signal (CPU/NET) and require multi-signal confirmation before emergency-fallback.
